card: This PR unifies the error message returned when raw transaction deserialization fails across eight RPC methods by defining a shared `TX_DECODE_ERROR_HINT` constant. It broadens the hint beyond missing inputs to mention serialization and hex encoding, and modifies multi-transaction RPCs to report the failing index rather than echoing raw transaction hex. It also adds test coverage for malformed and truncated transaction payloads in sendrawtransaction.
changed_since_previous: Added explicit functional test coverage for malformed, truncated, and padded transaction payloads in `test/functional/rpc_rawtransaction.py`.
evidence: PR description: "The 'Make sure the tx has at least one input.' advice is copied into every DecodeHexTx() error, even though that message also fires on bad hex and truncated or padded serialization. This moves the advice into one shared constant so the eight RPCs using it can't drift."
problem: RPC endpoints invoking `DecodeHexTx()` used copy-pasted, drifting error messages that specifically blamed missing inputs even when the failure was caused by invalid hex, truncated serialization, or extraneous bytes.

risk.why: Alters RPC error message strings for transaction deserialization failures, which could break external tools or scripts that parse error text instead of JSON-RPC error codes.

summary: Unifies the error message returned when raw transaction decoding fails across eight RPC methods by introducing a shared constant `TX_DECODE_ERROR_HINT`. Array-based RPCs (`generateblock`, `testmempoolaccept`, `submitpackage`, and `combinerawtransaction`) are updated to report the failing transaction index instead of echoing raw transaction hex back in the error message.
